domestic_evidence: Domestic supply activity is documented on the company's own live site https://www.hecltd.com/ : 'NCLT order, intimating CIRP of M/s. Heavy Engineering Corporation Private Limited and the Public Announcement requesting for the claims in the HEC Website' and 'Notice regarding submission of claims by Creditors under CIRP-21.11.2026'. The site also carries a live 'Tenders' section and 'Bill Status' portal, and describes HEC as 'a scheduled A CPSE' with operating units for steel plant equipment, mining equipment (electric rope shovels, draglines), crushing equipment and machine tools — i.e. an operating manufacturer with an active order/tender pipeline, not a shell. Note: this is evidence of an operating domestic business and of an active insolvency process, not a GST turnover figure or a specific GeM/CPPP contract award; no GSTIN turnover band or contract number was publicly retrievable in this session.
note: Legal name mismatch to flag: the claim 'HEAVY ENGINEERING CORPORATION PRIVATE LIMITED' matches the entity named in the NCLT/CIRP notice on hecltd.com, but the operating public-sector entity is 'Heavy Engineering Corporation Limited' (a CPSE, Ranchi, Jharkhand) — the 'Private Limited' form appears in the insolvency public announcement, so the two names may refer to the same corporate person post-conversion or to the CIRP-named entity; this needs registry confirmation (out of scope here). CRITICAL per Rule 3: HEC is under CIRP — NCLT admission order and public announcement dated 21.11.2026 are published on its own homepage, with creditor claim forms B–F. That is a formal insolvency commencement, which is the one ground on which rejection is permitted; the decision is for the reviewer, not for this evidence pass. Declared HS codes 820110 (hand tools, spades/shovels) and 847420 (crushing/grinding machines) are only partly consistent with the product range: 847420 fits the gyratory/cone/hammer crushers and rod mills, but 820110 (hand spades and shovels) does not describe HEC's electric rope shovels and draglines, which are HS 8429/8430 class heavy earth-moving machinery — the HS code should be corrected to the actual shipped goods rather than used as a rejection ground (Rule 3). Industry label 'Авиастроение и транспорт' (aircraft/transport) is not supported by anything seen: HEC's published business areas are steel plant equipment, mining equipment, machine tools, castings/forgings and cranes, with 'Special Purpose Railway Machine Tools' the only transport-adjacent line. Revenue and export volume: null — no public figure was retrievable in this session; not estimated.
